title: From case availability to staged expert-method replay
old_model: A source-backed case corpus and a blind split could be treated as if the system had already reproduced the expert's reasoning method.
observed_limitations: Target-palace evidence is not a full chart.
Retrieval and action selection readiness do not establish that the correct procedural method was applied.
A source outcome or expert prose can leak into blind evaluation if identities and source conclusions are not separated.
current_model: Represent corpus inventory, blind-safe evidence materialization, retrieval readiness, action-selection readiness, full expert replay, method-fidelity evaluation and predictive evaluation as separate maturity stages. The current 24-case readiness record stops before full expert replay.
rationale: The accepted Wang artifacts explicitly report 24/24 target-palace materialization and retrieval/action-selection readiness but 0/24 full expert replay readiness.
consequences: Materialize full charts and bind method patterns to case target scopes before claiming replay.
Keep source identities, expert reasoning, conclusions, outcomes and external biography out of blind views.
Use the first benchmark to test method reconstruction, not real-world predictive accuracy.
what_remains_valid: The 24 source cases and LOCO split are useful structured assets.
Target-palace facts can support bounded retrieval/action-selection diagnostics.
The method-policy readiness file is useful for identifying blockers, not as a performance score.

provenance.note: State cache itself says it is as of an earlier Product commit; live issues and accepted main artifacts remain authoritative.

boundaries: Provisional research-method framing; not a canonical rule or completed benchmark result.
